newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Feb 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Feb 7.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- DEVELOPERS WARN OVER TAX PLANS FOR LEASE FINANCING

Bankers and developers have warned the government that proposed changes to tighten the tax rules on lease financing have endangered billions of pounds of development projects. The government plans are designed to save 150 million stg a year lost to the Inland Revenue as a result of 'abusive leases', but, warn the bankers, the measure would also affect big projects such as the 600 million stg Bluewater shopping complex in Kent, or inward investments from firms such as Nissan or Siemens.
-- CHEAP LOANS ON OFFER IN RETURN FOR STUDYING FINANCE

High street banks participating in the Golden Key scheme, under which small businesses whose owners or managers complete financial training courses become eligible for cut-price loans, say it may be extended to the whole of the UK. Presently the scheme, which is supported by NatWest, Lloyds/TSB, Barclays, Midland and the Royal Bank of Scotland, and which is organised by the Business Links network, is undergoing a pilot project in Norfolk, Suffolk and south Derbyshire.
-- EURO CONVERSION COSTS 'NEGLIGIBLE'

A report published Thursday by the International Securities Market Association, the trade body of the securities industry, has claimed that banks and financial institutions have overestimated the costs of switching to a single European currency. The report found that financial institutions were spending on average about 0.058 per cent of total operating costs to convert to the euro, compared to the 2 per cent suggested by the European Banking Federation.
-- FORD STANDS FIRM OVER HALEWOOD DECISION

Ford has confirmed its intention to concentrate production of the next generation of its Escort model on plants in Spain and Germany, and to cut 1,300 jobs at the Halewood plant on Merseyside which produces the current model. The confirmation came in a meeting called by unions representing the Halewood workers, who have expressed strong support for strike action in protest at the planned job cuts.
-- CABLETEL CLAIMS BBC RENEGED ON DIGITAL DEAL

US cable company International CableTel, which is bidding to launch digital terrestrial television in the UK, has suggested that the BBC reneged on an understanding that it would support CableTel's application to the Independent Television Commission. CableTel received a letter from the Corporation indicating its support for their bid, but the understanding was later withdrawn after the BBC decided to link up with cable and satellite programming company Flextech in a joint venture to launch up to eight new subscription channels.
-- NEW CAR REGISTRATIONS OFF TO FLYING START

Figures published by the Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders reveal that new car registrations in the UK in January reached the second-highest total for the month on record. The statistics showed a total of 206,784 new cars were registered, an increase of 7.8 per cent on the same month last year. Imports accounted for 65.4 per cent of the total, compared to 60.9 per cent last time.
-- ICI TO FLOAT UNPROFITABLE PIGMENTS ARM

Chemicals group ICI has announced plans to float its unprofitable pigments business Tioxide in a move which it hopes will raise over 700 million stg. ICI claims the net asset value of Tioxide is about 700 million stg, with City analysts estimating the value of the company at between 400 million stg and 700 million stg. The surprise move to sell off Tioxide follows a year in which ICI saw its underlying pre-tax profits fall by one third to 603 million stg.
-- BT'S GERMAN ALLIANCE SIGNS NORWEGIAN ALLY

British Telecom has revealed that Norwegian telecoms company Telenor is to join its Viag Interkom joint venture in the German telecoms market. Telenor will pay an undisclosed amount for a 10 per cent stake in the alliance, which also involves German conglomerate Viag. The news came as BT announced third quarter results at the top end of expectations, with pre-tax profits for the three months to December 31 at 909 million stg, a rise of 9.7 per cent. Turnover for the period was up 4 per cent, at 3.76 billion stg.
-- VIRTUALITY REQUESTS SHARE SUSPENSION

Virtuality Group, the virtual reality pioneer, has requested an immediate suspension of its shares 'pending clarification of the group's financial position'. The board of Virtuality has said that all options are being explored as the company suffers severe cashflow problems following a sharp downturn in its arcade games business. Philips, IBM and Motorola all have small strategic stakes in Virtuality, though Philips has dismissed suggestions that it may now raise its stake in the company.
-- RAMCO IN BOOK BUILDING MOVE

Ramco Energy has announced plans to raise up to $115 million via the US practice of 'book building'. Ramco, the Aim-listed oil services and development company, is the second UK firm this week to announce it is using the US method to raise new capital. Details of the plans came as Ramco announced its 1996 results, which showed an increase in pre-tax profits from 750,000 stg to 870,000 stg, on turnover up from 6.9 million stg to 8.2 million stg.
